patients.label: 45-year-old man with severe treatment-resistant unipolar depression

identity_evidence.quote: A 45-year-old man was admitted to the acute male psychiatric unit in early July following ingestion of household bleach with suicidal intent.

attribution_limitations: Partner versus wife: b00008 says "his partner" and b00010 says "his wife".
The "2 antidepressants at therapeutic doses and durations" are not named; the abstract lists citalopram, mirtazapine and fluoxetine as trials.
The parenthetical "(early August)" follows the fluoxetine up-titration to 40 mg; it could also date the add/stop events.
Whether mirtazapine was stopped when fluoxetine was added, and whether citalopram or fluoxetine continued alongside lamotrigine, is not stated.
Lamotrigine start date and exact titration schedule are not given; only "weekly titration" and the 50 mg twice daily dose within 3 weeks.

Authors state the improvement was not achieved with antidepressants alone and the PHQ-9 reduction is "strong objective evidence"; this is author interpretation of a single case, and no explicit remission is stated for the patient.
The anchor of "Two weeks later" for the bleach ingestion (A&E attendance, start of Home Treatment Team care, or mirtazapine start) is not explicit.

limitations: Source gives months only (early March, mid-June, early July, early August, mid-September) without years or days; no calendar dates are recorded.
Follow-up is limited to about 3 weeks after lamotrigine initiation; no later outcome, discharge or relapse information.
Lamotrigine start date, intermediate titration and concurrent antidepressants are not stated.
Single case report; authors' causal attribution of improvement to lamotrigine is not independently supported.
